subject.title: [Bug]: Enabling Codex plugin causes Runtime to switch to OpenAI Codex and ignore configured primary model, resulting in GPT-5.4-nano TPM failures

question: Should #99449 be fixed first as a narrow stale OpenAI route/session repair, folded into the broader #87957 shared session-state resolver, or treated as expected when the session explicitly selected OpenAI?
rationale: Source proves DeepSeek should not be claimed directly by the Codex harness, but the live report combines Codex hot reload, persisted selected model state, OpenAI Responses routing, and a later `/model openai` clarification, so automation should not choose the permanent session-state contract on its own.

options.title: Fix narrow route drift first
options.body: Repair stale auto OpenAI session pins and literal `openai` doctor ownership while keeping #87957 as the broader resolver tracker.

options.title: Fold into #87957
options.body: Use #87957 as the canonical owner and copy this DeepSeek/Codex hot-reload scenario into its acceptance criteria before closing this issue later.

options.title: Treat explicit OpenAI selection as expected
options.body: If maintainers decide the report is only an explicit `/model openai` session, keep Codex-for-OpenAI behavior and improve status or doctor messaging instead of changing routing.

recommendation.title: Fix narrow route drift first
recommendation.body: Repair stale auto OpenAI session pins and literal `openai` doctor ownership while keeping #87957 as the broader resolver tracker.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest combined history across OpenAI provider identity, Codex runtime defaulting, and session model resolution.
